data.closed: Finance Act 2012 retrospectively taxed indirect transfers of Indian assets through foreign companies. The Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021 (assented 13 Aug 2021) bars new demands for such transfers made before 28 May 2012 and cancels existing ones once conditions such as withdrawing litigation are met; tax collected is refunded without interest.

data.closed: The India–Mauritius protocol (10 May 2016) gave India the right to tax gains on shares acquired from 1 April 2017 and grandfathered earlier holdings; the India–Singapore protocol (signed 30 Dec 2016) did the same. In Tiger Global (Jan 2026) the Supreme Court held that grandfathering and a residency certificate do not protect an arrangement lacking commercial substance.

data.closed: Press Note 2 (2018), issued 26 Dec 2018 and in force from 1 February 2019: a marketplace cannot own or control inventory; a vendor in which the marketplace group holds equity cannot sell on it; and if more than 25% of a vendor’s purchases come from the group, its inventory counts as controlled by the marketplace.
Section 3(d), as amended by the Patents (Amendment) Act, 2005, refuses new forms of known substances unless they show enhanced efficacy. The Supreme Court applied it in Novartis on 1 April 2013.

Google v DRS Logistics (2023): using a brand as a keyword is ‘use in advertising’ but not infringement by itself; it becomes infringement where it causes confusion, takes unfair advantage or harms the mark’s distinctiveness or repute. The court’s view that Google may not get safe harbour for its Ads programme was only prima facie.

data.closed: The CCPA treats such ads as misleading. On 21 August 2025 it fined Rapido ₹10 lakh for its ‘Auto in 5 min or get ₹50’ campaign and ordered it to pay the ₹50 to every customer who had not received it.

Pioneer Urban Land v Govindan Raghavan (Supreme Court, 2 April 2019) held such terms an unfair trade practice. The Consumer Protection Act, 2019, in force from 20 July 2020, also defines an ‘unfair contract’ that consumers can complain about.
The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 (in force 23 July 2020) police unfair trade practices online, and drip pricing became one of 13 specified dark patterns on 30 November 2023.
